# Kalasha Award for Best Host in a TV Show

| holder_label = Most recent winner

The Kalasha Award for Best Host in a TV Show (sometimes referred to as Best TV Host) is an annual television award presented by the Kenya Film Commission as part of the Kalasha International Film & TV Awards. It recognizes a presenter who has demonstrated outstanding charisma, audience engagement and professional delivery across reality, talk, lifestyle, or factual television programming.
The category was first introduced at the 2nd edition of the ceremony in 2010. It serves to honor the personalities who anchor Kenyan television, bridging the gap between production content and the viewing public.
The most recent recipient is Evelyn Wambui for her work on The Unspoken at the 13th edition held in 2024.
Criteria
To qualify for this award, a host must lead an unscripted or factual television program that was broadcast within the eligibility cycle. The Kalasha Academy evaluates nominees based on their interviewing techniques, on-screen presence and their ability to handle live or complex subjects with poise.
The selection process is governed by a weighted balloting system intended to synthesize professional critique with viewer loyalty. A technical review by the Kalasha Academy, consisting of broadcast veterans and media scholars, accounts for 70% of the final tally. The public decides the remaining 30% through a popular vote on official digital platforms, reflecting the host's influence and connection with the Kenyan audience.
Winners
The award ceremony was not held in 2009, 2013, 2016, 2023 and 2025. Winners are listed by year of ceremony.

Records
As of 2024, Jeff Koinange holds the record for the most awards in this category, reflecting his sustained impact on Kenyan talk show formats. Sarah Hassan also holds the distinction of winning for hosting in multiple ceremonies across her career.
Most awards
* Jeff Koinange – 2 awards (2010, 2019)
* Sarah Hassan  – 2 awards (2015, 2015)
